newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican guerrillas said to attack near capital.
newsitem.headline: Mexican guerrillas said to attack near capital.

text.p: The mysterious leftist guerrilla force known as the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) has attacked two military targets in central Mexico close to the capital, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The Mexico City newspaper La Jornada, citing anonymous guerrilla and army sources, said the attacks took place on Monday night and caused as many as nine casualties.
They would be the first incidents of guerrilla activity since the EPR ended a month-long unilateral truce on Sunday.
The Defence Ministry would neither confirm nor deny the reports, saying it had no information.

Citing unnamed Defence Ministry sources, La Jornada said the EPR injured one soldier late Monday when it attacked army barracks in Teotihuacan, near the famous pyramids an hour's drive northeast of Mexico City.

Early Monday, in Ocoyoacac, a forested area 10 miles (16 km) east of Mexico City, the army suffered "three casualties" in a rebel ambush, La Jornada said. It was not clear whether the soldiers were killed or injured.
But the EPR said there were eight casualties at Ocoyoacac, according to La Jornada, which said it received a phone call from an anonymous rebel spokesman.
If confirmed, the attacks would be a new show of force by the four-month-old guerrilla group.

The EPR first unveiled itself June 28 in a poor rural hamlet in southwestern Guerrero state and appears to have strength in rural Oaxaca state. Both states feature widespread poverty and remote, tree-covered mountains, conditions ideal for guerrilla activity.
The EPR also has appeared in Hidalgo, Puebla, Tabasco and Chiapas states in addition to the central state of Mexico where the latest reported attacks took place.
But apart from one spectacular operation in several states in late August, the EPR limited itself to minor ambushes.

La Jornada said the EPR was behind an attack on an office of the federal Attorney General in Guerrero state early Tuesday. The government said the office was shot up, receiving 57 bullet impacts from assault rifles, but did not say who was responsible. No casualties were reported.
